mlcommons.01.quote: MLCommons is an industry consortium backed by several dozen tech firms
mlcommons.01.note: Member dues are the only revenue base named and the working-group contributor list includes Amazon, Anthropic, Google, Google DeepMind, Meta FAIR, Microsoft and OpenAI, i.e. every major lab: cap 1 (F.5). The home page says "MLCommons is supported by over 125 members and affiliates"; per-member dues are not disclosed. A published share below 50% would lift this to 2.

mlcommons.02.quote: The Official Test dataset is private to avoid SUTs “gaming” the benchmark
mlcommons.02.note: Grading code (ModelBench) and a Creative Commons DEMO prompt set are open; the Official Test prompts are private: tasks partly open, 3 (M.1, M.3). A 4 needs open tasks plus documented third-party re-runs or factsheets. Stored 4 would move to 3.

mlcommons.03.quote: AVERI, OpenMined, and MLCommons were not able to see the model’s weights
mlcommons.03.note: The deepest documented engagement is running held-out prompts against a released model (Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite) inside an enclave that hid the weights from MLCommons: public-API-equivalent access, anchor 0 (A.1). No pre-release or safeguards-off access is documented. Stored 2 would move to 0 unless a lab-granted pre-release run is documented.

mlcommons.04.quote: MLCommons is supported by over 125 members and affiliates
mlcommons.04.note: Member-governed 501(c)(6) consortium (ProPublica) whose working group includes the labs benchmarked (Anthropic, Google, Meta, OpenAI among AILuminate contributors): cap 2 (G.4).

mlcommons.05.quote: designed and developed by the MLCommons AI Risk and Reliability working group
mlcommons.05.note: Self-directed benchmark design with no engagement to refuse floors at 3 (S.5). S.6 (co-authoring with the labs being evaluated) independently caps at 3 because lab employees sit in the working group; not added as a separate signal since the value is 3 either way.

mlcommons.06.note: Grades are published for named systems, but nothing states who reviews them before publication: "publishes" alone floors at 2 (R.7). A 3 needs a statement of no lab review or security-only redactions disclosed (R.1); R.5 needs an adverse finding beyond a ranking, and a "Poor" grade is a ranking. Stored 3 would move to 2 until MLCommons publishes its pre-publication review policy for SUT vendors.

mlcommons.07.quote: People from the following organizations have collaborated within the working group
mlcommons.07.note: Lab employees (Amazon, Anthropic, Cohere, Google, Google DeepMind, Meta FAIR, Microsoft, OpenAI are listed) sit in the working group that designs the benchmark: cap 2 (P.4, employee of a lab in a governing role, regardless of recusal).

mlcommons.08.quote: publicly released the AILuminate DEMO prompt dataset, a collection of 1,200 prompts
mlcommons.08.note: Open, free benchmark tooling: 3 (X.4). Document request: whether Official Test runs and the Global Assurance Program (with Google, Microsoft, Qualcomm, KPMG) are paid by the vendors tested; a paid run for a lab would be X.2.

mlcommons.09.quote: Peter Mattson is a senior staff engineer at Google. He founded and is President of MLCommons
mlcommons.09.note: A board member and president who is an employee of a lab caps at 2 regardless of recusal (P.4). Not P.1: he holds a job at the lab, not a governance seat. Added the leadership page (self, confirmed) so the cap is admissible under the standard policy.

dissent.lower: Funding (F) at 1 could be 0. The consortium was convened by Google engineers, its president is a Google senior staff engineer, and Google is a founding participant; the benchmarked labs sit in the working group that writes the benchmark and pay the dues that fund it. Anchor 0 covers an organization controlled by a frontier developer; a member-governed body whose president draws a Google salary is arguably that.
dissent.higher: Funding (F) at 1 could be 2. More than 125 members and affiliates pay dues, most of them chipmakers, universities and non-profits rather than frontier labs, and no member is documented above a trivial share. The AI Verify Foundation co-funded AILuminate. Lab dues beside a broad disclosed base is the anchor-2 picture of diversified revenue rather than lab revenue as the principal source.

P: Request from MLCommons the board conflict-of-interest and recusal policy that applies to directors employed by member companies whose systems are benchmarked, including any recusal recorded for the President on AILuminate grading decisions.
